 Water rescues in Delaware County with passage of storm; hail piles, too

 Share on Facebook (Opens in new window) 
 Facebook 
 Share on X (Opens in new window)

 Edgmont Avenue in Parkside on Thursday after the storm. (COURTESY PHOTO)
 By Daily Times PUBLISHED: November 12, 2026 at 3:00 PM EST | UPDATED: November 12, 2026 at 5:48 PM EST Getting your Trinity Audio player ready... Heavy rain, lightning and hail marked the passage of a storm system on Thursday that resulted in some flooded intersections and rescues from vehicles.
 A National Weather Service-issued tornado watch was set to run until 7 p.m. but that was canceled by 4 p.m. A flash flood warning is still in effect until 6:45 p.m.
 The slow-moving storm entered from the west about 2 p.m. and crawled across the county. The PECO power outage number  remained below 100 customers in the county.
 The main problems were vehicles stranded in quickly rising waters and stuck on hail. Many of the rescues were in the western half of the county. Emergency radio traffic showed there were no injuries.
 Dispatches for fire stations ramped up after 2:30, then subsided with the water after 3 p.m.
 Thursday’s storm dumped hail in Parkside and elsewhere.
 Parkside Officer Doug Staffelbach said while Edgmont Avenue was closed between Upland and Forrestview from hail blocking the road. Police posted a photo on social media showing a pickup truck stuck in what at first glance looks to be a snowfall.
 Staffelbach said PennDOT worked to get the road reopened, there were no other issues in the community.
 Other spots in Delaware County were closed as well while the hail melted or was picked up.
 In Brookhaven, Police Chief Timothy Habich said:
 “We experienced significant side street flooding because storm drains became clogged with leaves and hail. Police personnel and highway department personnel were very busy getting the drains cleared.
 “Some buses were delayed arriving at The Christian Academy due to flooding outside their main entrance.
 “Our highway department was forced to move large amounts of hail from the roadway with a backhoe. The hail was several feet deep at Trimble Blvd and Swiftwater Lane.
 “We also had a tree on the wooded property of the Brookhaven Swim Club get struck by lightning. The tree caught fire following the strike, and the Brookhaven Fire Department responded to evaluate.
 “I managed to get of the hail piled up in the road on Trimble Blvd.”
 COURTESY OF BROOKHAVEN POLICE 
 The precipiation total at Philadelphia International Airport at 4:30 p.m. was up to 0.51 inch. It doesn’t say how much of that was rainfall and how much was hail that melted in the cup.
 Other totals available at 4:30 p.m. through the MesoWest collaborative showed an Upper Chichester spotter at 0.95 inch, with Swarthmore at 0.92, and several others that were far lower.
 The weather service says to expect rain at times through the night with the temperature diving to the low 40s by daybreak Friday. Then the forecast is for rain to continue at times Friday with a high in the mid-to-upper 40s as a cold front nears.
 That front should cross the region late Friday into Saturday morning and a blustery and cold day is expected, though with clearing skies.
 Starting Sunday, moderation will be in order as the forecast daily highs climb through the 50s to 60 on Wednesday and sunny conditions hold, the forecast shows.
